#Bitcoin – What’s Next?

The Big Sunday Report: All We Need to Know

TA / LCA / Psychological Breakdown:

I remain bullish on the opportunity in front of us. If you turn time back, I was bullish in July at 60-64k, and guess who was bearish back then? All the bears that are bearish in these days, and the bears back then missed the entire run to 87k, and now we returned back to the exact place where it all started, and for some reason the bears celebrate the recent move, as if something would have changed for them. I  acknowledge that my recent long trade from $80K did not work as expected. That does not mean I become bearish on Bitcoin. As we speak the Fear & Greed Index has fallen to 10, reaching EXTREME FEAR. This is precisely when I become interested in accumulation again for the long term. Remember, there is a difference between trading which can be done at any price, and long term investing that should be done at potential market bottoms, spot positions that are built for the next 2-3 years, and we just returned to the area I am interested to buy for the long term, rather than focusing on trading. 

Bitcoin is massively oversold on the DAILY chart. The daily RSI reached approximately 19 which shows extreme over sold levels. The weekly RSI is around 43, which is slightly oversold on the Weekly. But what is interesting now on the chart is the triple bottom on the daily RSI that marked the local bottom precisely in the last months, as you can see in the chart. This would be one of the arguments to say , a local bottom is forming here, but there are more arguments to follow.

Lets have a look at the mining-cost for BTC, other words for its production, same as if you need to produce a chair, BTC has a production cost level as well. A production-cost estimate published earlier this month placed the cost around $61,200. For referrence, in June 2022, Glassnode estimated production costs around $17,200, while Bitcoin bottomed at 16,400 in the last bear market, nearby the production cost level. Historically, it turned out to be always very profitable to invest close to the Bitcoin production cost basis. 

Also, there was a very big liquidation cluster around $62K on the 6 month chart. Now I have a question about what happened on this Saturday: The person who sold Millions worth of Bitcoin, could have done so at higher volume moments, like during weekdays, he could have easily sold in smaller batches at 68k and the market would not have reacted much because of the higher volume. Why hit a thin market, on purpose during weekend with aggressive market selling, pushing Bitcoin from $68K toward $62K, almost 9% within hours? Exactly to the area where most of liquidations are located. I smell intention here. My interpretation is that the liquidation cluster was the target, it was wicked once for it so there might be another push for it and this is why I believe this area is the bottom.

My focus remains the same as in July this year. I am interested to expand my spot positions in the area of $60K–$64K region. Join Free Telegram: https://t.me/Therealdrprofit

THIS IS NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE, BUT EDUCATIONAL CONTENT ONLY.

In total, $BTC has lost $16B in open interest in 10 days.

But denominated in coins, it is still near yearly highs and barely came off relative for the move we've seen. (This means most of the OI lost was simply the underlying asset depreciating).

We've not seen as many actual liquidations as one would expect with such a violent non-stop down move.

This often means there's still a lot of volatility and liquidations ahead (this can be both ways).

tweets.text:
I think by now it is consensus that we did see one or more major entities sell out of billions of $BTC last week. 

Especially considering this sell pressure kept going into the weekend. This makes it seem more like forced selling by some fund that blew up than actual "organic" selling pressure. No one would choose to sell that much during a weekend when you'd get a worse executing price if there was no time pressure.

So it was either forced selling or an informed seller trying to frontrun something. Most selling happened on Coinbase.

Let's assume there's no insider trading at play for the sake of this. If it was indeed forced selling during a weekend from some fund that blew up, then that would be one of those rare opportunities in the market and would likely see us retrace back to $70K+ very quickly. Historically those were the dumps to bid.

So watch very closely these days to see if the coinbase discount starts diminishing and funding rates to also go negative possibly. That'd be a good indication that the heavy spot selling is done and spot buyers instead are stepping in.

quote.text:
$BTC With how this has been trading I am pretty confident of my previous statement that there's likely been one or more major whales offloading billions of Bitcoin at a rapid pace.

(Yes I know this might be stating the obvious as clearly we had a lot of selling after such a move. The point I want to make is that it is likely some large unknown seller(s) that have been dumping BTC specifically).

Some things I'm seeing:
1. Funding has remained at its highs regardless of the "down only" price action.
2. The Coinbase discount has been at multi year lows for several weeks.
3. Shorts have been hammering price and have not been punished much.
4. Price has been completely ignoring any big up days in the stock market.
5. The past few days especially we've seen some majors have hold up better than BTC. This rarely happens during large corrections unless there's some major selling of BTC specifically going on.

If I had to guess, this sudden selling now comes from the fear of some major hack or exploit happening in the future. It is no secret that we're seeing a lot of that right now due to AI. For many (long term) investors it doesn't feel "safe" anymore to just hold your coins in your wallet. Whether it's exploits or quantum in the future, things don't feel as comfy as they were.

Obviously this is all just speculation from my side and it's not like we can do a lot with it at this point after the move has happened. The best you can do is watch for the Coinbase discount to slowly diminish from here on out and for funding rates to turn back down. That would indicate spot selling has stalled.

I also think that would be the cue for a lot of swing shorts that have been milking this move down from higher to start taking profit which should see the Open Interest come down a bit. Good game to those guys because that was an amazing trade.

As mentioned yesterday, the most scary down moves are the ones where there's no direct narrative or reason as to why. Often in hindsight we figure out that it was simply some large player offloading billions in coins. The market is still small enough for single large entities to have such an impact.

tweets.text:
Crypto won't bottom while people still feel comfortable.

And that's exactly what I'm seeing right now.

Despite the massive decline, there's still a strange sense of relief in the market.

People genuinely believe the worst is over.

But where is the fear? Where is the desperation? Where is the hopelessness I witnessed at previous cycle bottoms?

I don't see it.

When the real bottom arrives, I expect the sentiment to be absolutely brutal.

Nobody will want to buy. Nobody will believe in a recovery. Even those brave enough to accumulate will be mocked and ridiculed.

The same people begging for lower prices today will be too terrified to buy when they finally arrive.

That's how I believe this cycle will end.

Not with excitement.

With exhaustion, fear, and absolutely no hope left.

Hope you understand.

This is probably one of the scenarios I'll be discussing in more detail at @AlphaDoctrine_x 

I won't go too deep into it here. I'll just leave you with this chart and let you think about it.

The idea is fairly simple: a potential move into the $40K–$47K zone, followed by a prolonged accumulation phase before the next major expansion.

Obviously, we can't pull the trigger just because price reaches that zone.

I need to see specific market structures develop and confirmation that the conditions I'm looking for are actually there.

In my opinion, this is a very reasonable scenario.

The alternative? A much more aggressive move straight toward $30K.

Both remain on the table.

There's no need to predict every move in advance. We simply need to understand the possibilities, remain patient, and react when the market gives us the right conditions.

That's exactly the kind of analysis I want to take to another level with Alpha Doctrine.

Hope you understand.

Crypto has no shortage of information. What it lacks is clarity.

That’s why we built Alpha Doctrine by @Alejandro_XBT 

What it is

Alpha Doctrine is a private crypto research publication. We combine technical analysis with macroeconomic context to help our members read the market, understand what’s driving it and weigh the scenarios ahead.

Our goal isn’t to tell you what to do. It’s to help you build your own judgement, grounded in reasoning, structure and discipline.

What members get

At the core is The Doctrine Letter, our monthly publication. Each issue covers market structure, the macro forces behind price action and the scenarios we’re watching.

Between issues, members receive short market updates when something actually matters, along with access to our research library and a private members app.

For those who want closer access, our Direct membership adds a private Telegram community, the team’s portfolio journal, private indicators and asynchronous access to the team.

What we are not

We’re not a signals group. We don’t promise returns, and we don’t give personalised investment advice. We publish research and share our process openly. The decisions are always yours.

The waitlist is open

Alpha Doctrine is in pre-launch, and memberships will open soon. Join the waitlist to be among the first to get access when they do:

http://alphadoctrine.io

Think beyond the noise.

What a crazy coincidence! 🤯

Q1 2025

▫️ Bitcoin peaked in early Jan.
▫️ Dropped 30% in 7 weeks
▫️ Bybit got hacked.
▫️ Nasdaq dropped 14%.

Q4 2026

▫️ Bitcoin peaked in early October.
▫️ Dropped 29% in 7 weeks
▫️ Binance got hacked.
▫️ Nasdaq dropped 16%.

In Q1 2025, Bitcoin underperformed stocks during its first major dump, just like now.

Then, BTC had a recovery and final drop in April 2025, almost 4% below the March low.

Meanwhile, Nasdaq dropped another 15% from its March low and entered a bear market correction.

If this repeats, BTC will bottom around $59K-$60K, while Nasdaq will drop below 24,500.

tweets.text:
A Bitcoin trading strategy I’m looking to deploy this week (in tandem with what I already have) is the following:

•  $50,000 budget
•  4 attempts
•  $12,500 of margin per trade with 5x leverage ($62,500 position size)

Each trade would be liquidated on a ~20% drop from its entry price:

•  Entry 1 at $64,000 → liquidation at $51,000
•  Entry 2 at $51,000 → liquidation at $40,700
•  Entry 3 at $40,700 → liquidation at $32,300
•  Entry 4 at $32,300 → liquidation at $24,100

My expectation is that I would be highly likely to catch the BTC low with Entry 1 or Entry 2.

Assuming that is the case and Bitcoin reclaims (at a minimum) its prior $126,000 all-time high:

•  With Entry 1 I would make ~$60,547
•  With Entry 2 (net, after the liquidated Entry 1 margin) I would make ~$79,412

In the worst-case scenario of needing Entry 4 (after losing the first three $12,500 margins), the net profit would be ~$143,808.

The majority of $BTC spot selling is happening on Coinbase, which is visible in massive ETF outflows.

One reason behind this could be Anthropic's upcoming IPO, for which investors are selling Bitcoin.

We saw a similar dump in BTC before the SpaceX IPO too.

Such dumps are usually very aggressive, and it takes time for the market to build a base.

I don't think a V-shaped recovery is possible from here, and we'll see more chop just like July/August before the next leg up.
